title: Corned Beef Plate Pie
subtitle: A Northern English plate pie of tinned corned beef and potato
excerpt: Tinned corned beef and soft onion potato filling, sandwiched between two layers of shortcrust pastry on a dinner plate. A thrifty, nostalgic tea-time pie.
sourceNotes: Northern English working-class cookery tradition; the plate pie format traces to domestic cooks using dinner plates instead of pie dishes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool fully, wrap in foil and freeze for up to three months. Reheat at 180C from frozen until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made a day ahead and kept in the fridge. Assemble and bake just before serving.

content.text: Corned beef plate pie is a storecupboard classic with almost no prep. The filling sets firm as it bakes, so the pie slices cleanly. Watch the edges: the top pastry can lift away if you skip the egg seal.

items.prepNote: half for the base, half for the lid
one standard tin, roughly broken up

content.text: Boil the potato in salted water for 12 minutes until tender. Drain well and leave to cool.
Melt the butter in a pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for eight minutes until soft. Remove from the heat.
Combine the corned beef, potato, cooked onion and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl. Mash together roughly, keeping some texture. Season with salt and pepper. Leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Divide the pastry in half. Roll one piece out and use it to line the pie dish.
Spoon in the filling and press it down into an even layer.
Roll the second piece of pastry for the lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg and lay the lid on. Press and seal the edges, then trim.
Score a few small slits in the top and brush with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden. Rest for five minutes before cutting.

items.cause: The corned beef released fat during baking.
items.fix: Drain any visible fat from the corned beef before mixing. Pat the potato dry before adding it.

items.symptom: The top layer slides off when slicing.
items.cause: The egg seal was too thin or the rim was greasy.
items.fix: Brush the rim generously and press the edges firmly. Crimp with a fork for extra grip.

items.symptom: The pastry cracks across the top.
items.cause: The filling was still warm and steamed the pastry from inside.
items.fix: Cool the filling completely before assembling. Warm filling always cracks the lid.
